lines.text: Same list. Same code. I only changed where the nodes sit in memory.
Two linked lists, with the same ten million nodes. One chained in memory order, the other shuffled. The code just adds up the values.
On the sequential one, the sum takes about thirty milliseconds. On the shuffled one, over two seconds. Eighty to ninety times slower.
With a thousand nodes, nothing changes. With a hundred thousand, it's already ten times or more.
Same sum, same structure. Want to know why? Comment below. Code in the description.
